question: Does an explicit learned strategic repertoire deserve to exist, before any latent-conditioned policy is trained?
why_this_gate_exists: V3 validation established that the environment ADMITS a valuable two-mode solution. It did NOT establish that learning discovers or needs one. PPO could still converge on a single adequate compromise policy. That is a separate failure mode, answered by training rather than by the scripted confirmation.

R1_train_three_policies.compute_fairness: the generalist receives 2T steps because the repertoire consumes 2T total (T + T). This forecloses the obvious objection that the repertoire won by spending twice the environment interaction.

training_seeds.note: disjoint blocks, audited; PopulationTrainer per-member offsets up to 300 are covered by 320-wide reservations

R1_train_three_policies.mandatory_precondition: assert on the LIVE core object that pole A's overlay (min_alive_for_defender=2) is applied before any training step is consumed. Training against plain OP6 by accident would invalidate the entire ladder.

R2_learned_payoff_matrix.matrix: rows {pi_G, pi_A, pi_B} x columns {A, B}

gate_learned_crossover.pairing: both policies evaluated on the SAME untouched evaluation seeds within each pole; paired bootstrap over seed-level differences, the repository's established procedure
gate_learned_crossover.deliberately_no_magnitude_floor: R2 asks only 'did PPO learn complementary best responses?'. Statistical directional crossover answers that. The value floor belongs in R3. Putting a second magnitude threshold in R2 would measure value twice.
gate_learned_crossover.if_fails: STOP. The environment contains the strategies but PPO is not discovering complementary ones. A legitimate, publishable result directing work to LEARNING, not latent compression.

R3_oracle_repertoire_value.threshold_provenance: reused from the campaign's earlier repertoire-value standard (delta_pool floor 0.05), NOT invented after seeing results
R3_oracle_repertoire_value.explicitly_not_deployment_valid: the oracle secretly knows which opponent it faces. Because A and B are deliberately concealed, oracle routing CHEATS. This establishes repertoire EXISTENCE only and is reported as an upper-bound diagnostic.
R3_oracle_repertoire_value.if_fails: STOP. No repertoire value even with perfect routing.
R3_oracle_repertoire_value.unlocks: LATENT COMPRESSION IS JUSTIFIED. If two complementary learned policies collectively contain more value than one learned policy, then 'can pi(a|o,z) preserve that repertoire inside one network?' is a well-posed question.

R5_memory_control_before_claiming_latent.requirement: compare a recurrent / event-conditioned PPO against the explicit repertoire
R5_memory_control_before_claiming_latent.distinguishes: 'memory solves it' from 'persistent strategic modes provide additional value'
R5_memory_control_before_claiming_latent.status: required for publication-quality claims that LATENT specifically is necessary; not a blocker for running the latent experiment itself

latent_gate.unlocked_only_if: R2 crossover AND R3 oracle value pass. R4 is informative about deployment but is NOT a precondition for latent compression work.
latent_gate.then: train pi(a|o,z), z in {0,1}, z sampled ONCE at episode start and held FIXED for the episode
latent_gate.why_fixed_z: matches the persistent-strategy hypothesis and prevents z from degenerating into an instantaneous tactical router, which is what the earlier failed attempts produced
latent_gate.reframed_question: not 'please become different somehow' but 'compress two already-proven-useful strategic responses into one shared network'
measurements: does the latent mixture match the explicit population
how much is lost by compressing two policies into one shared network

stop_rules: R2 crossover fails -> STOP, learning problem, not a latent problem
R3 oracle value fails -> STOP, no repertoire value even with perfect routing
R4 mixture fails -> repertoire exists and has oracle value, but blind selection/routing is the bottleneck; latent compression remains allowed by R2+R3
no threshold may be moved after seeing any result
no extension of any evaluation block
prohibited: training a latent-conditioned policy before R2 and R3 pass
using opponent identity as a policy input anywhere except the explicitly-labelled R3 oracle diagnostic
changing the benchmark environment in any way
giving the repertoire more total environment interaction than the generalist

PI_DECISIONS_2026_08_18.T_anchor: 1M is the known competence scale from G0-V5
PI_DECISIONS_2026_08_18.seeds: ONE canonical training seed per policy. Three-seed training is NOT reintroduced.

checkpointing.prohibited: cherry-picking an intermediate checkpoint after seeing evaluation. Intermediate checkpoints are diagnostics.

PI_DECISIONS_2026_08_18.ppo_config: the exact G0-V5 configuration (architecture, optimizer, rollout, GAE, entropy/value coefficients, normalization, observation pipeline, reward V5, gamma 0.995)

FORCED_DELTAS_FROM_G0_V5_READ_THIS.issue: 'exact G0-V5 preset' cannot be literal. G0-V5 trained under RULESET_V2_AQUATICUS_10S against an OP6-OP12 mixture. The frozen V3 benchmark REQUIRES RULESET_V3_M1.

forced_deltas.1_ruleset: RULESET_V2_AQUATICUS_10S -> RULESET_V3_M1 (own_flag_home_required_to_score=True). MANDATED by V3_BENCHMARK_FROZEN, not a tuning choice.
forced_deltas.2_opponents: admitted OP6-OP12 mixture -> pole A only / pole B only / balanced 50-50 A,B

everything_else_nailed_down: reward V5 (locked_reward_v5 block, sparse_flag_capture_points=100.0, sparse_own_oob_points=-70.0, win/lose/draw 1.0/-1.0/-0.5, gamma 0.995)
tag telemetry enabled through production PPOConfig

risk_flagged.what: G0-V5's competence-at-1M evidence was gathered under RULESET_V2 against a 7-opponent mixture. Neither condition holds here.
risk_flagged.direction_unclear: single fixed opponent is usually EASIER than a 7-opponent mixture (less diversity to cover), which argues 1M is ample. But M1 changes the scoring condition (own flag must be home to score), which could slow credit assignment.
risk_flagged.mitigation: checkpoint cadence 100000 gives a learning curve. If a policy is plainly not competent at its terminal budget, the curve will show it and that is itself a reportable result -- NOT grounds to silently extend training or to score an intermediate checkpoint.
risk_flagged.not_a_reason_to_change_T: T is frozen. If 1M proves insufficient, that is a finding to report, not a parameter to quietly raise.

R4_opponent_blind_mixture_THE_REAL_TEST.why_this_is_separate: because A and B are concealed before commitment, a legitimate repertoire cannot know which specialist to deploy. This asks whether an explicit population provides value under the SAME uncertainty the generalist faces; it is a deployment/selection test, not the latent-compression gate.
R4_opponent_blind_mixture_THE_REAL_TEST.procedure: sample the policy ONCE before the episode from a fixed mixture P(pi_A)=p, P(pi_B)=1-p, with NO access to opponent identity, then commit for the whole episode
R4_opponent_blind_mixture_THE_REAL_TEST.p_selection: chosen from a SEPARATE development payoff matrix on block 7600001..7600192, then FROZEN before touching the evaluation block
R4_opponent_blind_mixture_THE_REAL_TEST.if_passes: multiple learned strategic policies are useful without cheating on opponent identity; selection succeeds under concealment.
R4_opponent_blind_mixture_THE_REAL_TEST.if_fails: the repertoire exists and has oracle value, but selecting the right mode without opponent identity is the bottleneck.
R4_opponent_blind_mixture_THE_REAL_TEST.structural_note: this mirrors what a latent policy must ultimately do: sample z at episode start, commit, opponent identity stays hidden

CORRECTED_ROLE.is_NOT: the gate that decides whether latent work is allowed
CORRECTED_ROLE.is: a SELECTION / DEPLOYMENT question: can the repertoire be exploited WITHOUT privileged knowledge of the opponent, given the concealment we validated?
CORRECTED_ROLE.why_separate: R2 PASS + R3 PASS + R4 FAIL would NOT mean 'do not do latent'. It would mean the repertoire exists and has value, but selecting the right mode is hard -- a fascinating result precisely because we validated concealment.
CORRECTED_ROLE.keeps_R3_and_R4_distinct: R3 asks whether the repertoire is worth anything; R4 asks whether it can be deployed blind. Confusing them would muddle the paper.

R0_prerequisite.tests: experiments/test_opponent_spec.py plus tests/test_r1_training_contract.py; focused R0/R1/M1/formal-identity suite 29/29 passing
R0_prerequisite.path: clear override -> set base opponent -> apply intended overlay -> ASSERT resolved profile
R0_prerequisite.assertion_target: core._bt_resolved_profile_tensors(), the live object the behaviour tree actually reads -- not the override attribute, which can be set without reaching the tree
covered_failure_modes: A requested -> plain OP6 delivered (min_alive_for_defender 3 vs 2)
stale A override contaminating OP7 (caught on defender_zone_frac 0.35 vs 0.05, since min_alive_for_defender is 2 for BOTH pole A and OP7 and would miss it)
override lost on env.reset() or auto-reset
negative control: the assertion fires on both mismatch directions
R0_prerequisite.manifest: resolved opponent profile recorded per run; a run claiming A but resolving OP6 crashes loudly rather than producing a graph of the wrong experiment
R0_prerequisite.production_path: rl.training.orchestrator pre_rollout_env_setup runs after live env construction and before identity, artifacts, trainer construction, or rollout; experiments/run_r1_repertoire_training.py is the only R1 launcher
R0_prerequisite.mixed_batch_overlay: core._bt_profile_override is keyed by live opponent tag, so OP6 receives pole A and OP7 remains canonical across per-episode pool sampling
R0_prerequisite.m1_identity: RULESET_V3_M1_OWN_FLAG_HOME; M1 can no longer be stamped as RULESET_V2_AQUATICUS_10S

PI_G_OPPONENT_DISTRIBUTION_MEASURED.documented_intent_was: per-episode resampling from the opponent pool with weights (0.5, 0.5)
PI_G_OPPONENT_DISTRIBUTION_MEASURED.measured_behaviour: STATIC balanced split. Envs are assigned [OP6, OP7, OP6, OP7, ...] at construction and keep their pole for the whole run; across 75 env-terminations in a direct probe the composition never changed.
PI_G_OPPONENT_DISTRIBUTION_MEASURED.verified_before: pi_G consumed any of its 2M steps
scientifically_sound_because: every gradient batch is exactly 50/50 A/B, with no sampling noise
the policy is feedforward and cannot observe env index, so a static split is equivalent to a shuffled order
opponent identity remains invisible to the policy, as the protocol requires
PI_G_OPPONENT_DISTRIBUTION_MEASURED.consequence_for_contamination: the A<->B switch never occurs during pi_G, so there is no switch path for a stale overlay to corrupt. This is a stronger safety property than an assertion firing on each switch.
PI_G_OPPONENT_DISTRIBUTION_MEASURED.how_to_describe_it: pi_G trains on a fixed balanced 50/50 A/B split across parallel environments -- NOT per-episode opponent resampling. Describe it that way.
PI_G_OPPONENT_DISTRIBUTION_MEASURED.guard: tests/test_r1_training_contract.py asserts the split stays static and balanced. If the sampler ever starts re-sampling, that test fails and the keyed overlay must be re-verified across switches.
